Messages.Author: Olivier_PEREZ
Messages.Body:
Response from the Swiss Academy to the Open letter from Mike Tinne

http://groups.google.ch/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/browse_thread/thread/dbf0a832a3ed4e4a/024a474da1221aee?hl=fr&q=Mike+Tinney&lnk=ol&

Dear Mr. Tinney,

First of all we would like to thank you for the work you have
accomplished and are still doing for all of the VTES players. This
letter is our "open answer" to your "open letter" published just two
month ago. We took some time composing this not only because Swiss
people like to take their time but, also to give us the opportunity to
think about the practical side of the issue at two recent tournaments
in Prague and Germany. As you mentioned, not everything has been
perfect since the game's debut but, let us contribute with what we
believe is working for the game now.

What has been done so far:

Princes from all cities have done a great job with communication and
we can tell links are being created between playgroups worldwide. Not
only is it easy to join a prince, but it is also easy to find players
everywhere you go to. People seem to be motivated and show a lot of
goodwill facing communication tasks.

The game's merits:

1. One of the most important ones is the game's social dimension.
Indeed VTES is more than just a card game, it is a social game.
2. The connection with the World of Darkness adds a bit of fantasy to
the game and building your own deck according this vision can be very
rewarding. Yet the main interest of the game seems to reside in
developing and executing your strategies. Luck can be easily factored
as not relevant in this game.
3. The dynamic created by the five player's prey-predator relation
takes some heavy psychology to master. Table control is the art of
keeping everyone happy when actually only one player can win the
game.

The game's spirit:

We would like to emphasise here the overall sportsmanlike spirit that
predominates at international tournaments and which we specially
appreciate. To us, playing VTES means meeting players from just about
everywhere but, it also means making friends with your game's enemies,
sharing strategies. All this more social and "unprofessional" side of
the game is very valuable.
To us it seems important that huge sums of money stay out of the game
for, it would ruin the friendly spirit that makes tournaments
enjoyable. Also a very small difference in prizes between the winner
and the others avoids new player's frustration.

What could be improved:

Internal Policy: We could begin with having an internal policy
that ensures that any sent mail actually gets a reply within, say,
three weeks. Even if it's only a generic answer. What really matters
is that players know someone is lending them an ear and that their
query will be considered later on.

Playgroupvtes.com: Creating a tool to help you find your own town's
players seems necessary. Information could be provided that would
allow you to contact anyone that has ever signed in. It could, for
example, be a webpage like "playgroupvtes.com" offering every player
the possibility to be registered on his town's player list. But, to be
effective, the link to this player list needs to be reproduced on
every starter and booster. This way anyone buying cards would have an
easy way to find other players and start playing. As far as technical
tools are concerned, a last detail would be making the online Archon
easier to use.

Prize support, a travel opportunity: Changing the prize support system
could be very useful for connecting playgroups to each other. We could
think of prize support consisting of a flight, for instance the winner
of the CE could get a flight to go to the NAC.
It is then more than likely that many other players will, on their own
behalf, accompany the prized one.

Prince help database: Concerning the role of princes, these volunteers
could use some help with a guide to their activities: how to organise
a playgroup; how to organise a demo; how to organise a tournament.

A world championship: It would be very exciting if we could organise a
world championship. It would motivate most players and, be an
opportunity to have a major event. This could also help establish
relationships between the different playgroups.

Stability of the game: There is also an other aspect of the game
itself that could be improved; considering the fact the game is mostly
played by players between 20 and 35 years old, we could improve the
number of cards that are kept playable. Most players like the game
because they don't need to change the way they play every half a year.
Controlling the rhythm and quality of editions is crucial.

Play testing: We find it great that a European coordinator has been
named and we are looking forward to seeing the next step of this
evolution: which would be having European play testers. Since we seem
to approach the game slightly differently in Europe than in United
States it would only be normal that European players get to share
their vision on the cards of the next edition. This is why we proposed
ourselves to be play testers as part of this European VTES world.

These are the things we believe could be currently improved in VTES,
we hope our vision of the matter helps you getting new perspectives
and we look forward to keeping contact with you.

Best Regards,
Olivier Perez
Prince of Geneva
Headquarters of the Swiss Academy

This letter has been compose and written by:
Jens-Thilo Rumphorst Swiss National Coordinator
Gabriel Carnino
Pablo Carnino
Ruben Feldman current number 1 player
Mathias Matzler
Damien Wursten Prince of Lausanne
Thomas Piguet

People have gone to Hell for less, XZealot. ;)

RE: OP: A fairly reasonable response, and hopefully a good sign of
further support & communication to come. I'd especially stress the
importance of the social element. The problem with any game involving
'big money' (big being a very subjective term, of course) is that it
radically changes the state of the game. At the end of the day, people

game itself.

VTES is, imo, golden not because of the game itself, but because of
the community it created. The game just helped to foster that through
the mechanics of how it works.

date of signing, not the release date of the set.)

> Try to be realist.

While I am in no way opposed to adding an extra advertisement on a
booster, I'm being a realist. The rulebook already has information
about finding other players around you. The White Wolf website makes
it incredibly easy to do so.

The problem is not a lack of information.

> If it's written on all booster:
> find other player by contacting the prince of your city onwww.princevtes.com

This is on the WW website already. I mean, again, yeah, it would in no
way hurt anything to have a pointer on the booster wrappers. But
anyone already with a modicum of want to do so can easily locate
Princes and nearby playgroups and whatever. And the rulebook already
points to this information.

> Recently in Geneva we discoverd a knew playgroup that didn't know
> about the comunity and was playing for 10 years...

This isn't 'cause it is hard to find local playgroups and it isn't
'cause there wasn't readily available information that comes with the
cards. It is 'cause people are lazy and don't necessarily follow
instructions that come with their products if they don't feel it is
necessary to do so. If the local playgroup wanted to find out about
the community, they could have done so in 2 minutes on the internet
(if you type "vampire the eternal struggle" into google, the first
link is the WW VTES homepage, and from there, the world!).

Again, it is in no way a bad idea to have pointers on booster
wrappers. But really. The information is already there and already
available and already easy to access and already in the rulebook.

-Peter

> important information must be presented in a special way to attract
> their attention.

There is only so much you can do to make people do things. You could
tatoo a website address on every VTES player's forehead, and most folks
*still* wouldn't go to that website. As I said before, the problem that
you are trying to overcome here is not one of lack of information. It is
trying to overcome people's inertia. The information (i.e. how to find
other VTES players) is already easily available and dropped in people's
laps. If folks aren't going to a VTES website based on the information
in the rulebook, what makes you think they will go there based on
information printed on boosters?

Again, I'm in no way opposed to printing pointers on booster backs--it
costs nothing to do and requires no further infrastructure to be
established. But I think it is kind of foolish to think that it will
make a significant impact on people's habits. If folks aren't going to
see and use this information in the rulebook, why are they going to see
and use it on booster packs?

Currently, if someone who plays VTES is remotely interested in finding
other players, and have used a computer ever, they can find them in less
than 2 minutes (I just opened up google, typed "vampire the eternal
struggle", clicked on the first link, saw "player registry" and clicked
on that. Players from your city instantly.) This information is in the
rulebook even if you aren't savy enough to figure it out on your own.
Again, sure--put it on booster packs. It couldn't hurt in one bit. But
I'm unconvinced that it would have that significant of an impact on the
system at all. 'Cause people aren't finding neighboring playgroups due
to not being able to or not knowing how. It is 'cause they don't want to
be bothered for whatever reason. And if they don't want to be bothered,
they aren't going to suddenly want to be bothered by seeing a pointer on
a booster pack.

Peter D Bakija
